Whence, for our purpose, it would be an almost ridiculous thing, of pernicious and very bad example, that a man could make a debtor at his will, or otherwise prejudice him <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>. And that is why our Jurisconsults will not have credit given to one who is dying of a wound and charges another with having wounded him, if there is no proof from elsewhere <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>; although I would not deny that such a delation gives rise to some slight presumption against the one whom the dead man accuses <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>. For although, says Baldus, every man who is about to die is not St John the Evangelist, nevertheless it is not likely that he should be so wholly forgetful and so little mindful of his salvation, even at the extremity of his life <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>, as to wish to denounce another falsely <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>. I have said expressly "some slight presumption": for to say, with some, that the sole assertion of the murdered man, charging the accused, is sufficient indication for torture <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>, seems to me (I speak always under the censure of the more learned) to have neither sense nor appearance of reason. For besides that this manifestly contradicts and is repugnant to the words and reason of the laws which have spoken of it <sup class="mk" data-key="n">n</sup>, if it were true the wounded man would be a witness in his own cause, against the common decisions <sup class="mk" data-key="o">o</sup>; and nevertheless his testimony would be worth two, inasmuch as two witnesses are required to prove an indication for torture <sup class="mk" data-key="p">p</sup>; which would be, in one and the same matter, to introduce two special things, and far too irregular <sup class="mk" data-key="q">q</sup>. For the same reasons we say that if a witness, Judge or Notary, at the last breath of his life, confessed to having borne false witness <sup class="mk" data-key="r">r</sup>, pronounced a judgment <sup class="mk" data-key="ſ">ſ</sup>, or forged a false instrument <sup class="mk" data-key="t">t</sup>, for money or some other kind of corruption, credit would nonetheless not be given them to the prejudice of the party to whom the right was already acquired <sup class="mk" data-key="u">u</sup>. For the confession of one who is about to die cannot harm or prejudice another. lines: fant {e}. Dont à noſtre propos ce ſeroit vne choſe preſque
ridicule, de pernicieux & fort mauuais exemple, que
l'homme peuſt faire vn debiteur à ſa volõté, ou autre-
ment luy preiudicier {f}. Et voila pourquoy nos Iuriſ-
conſultes ne veulent point qu'on donne foy à celuy
qui ſ'en va mourir de bleſſeure, & charge vn autre de
l'auoir bleſſé, ſ'il n'y a preuue d'ailleurs {g}. Bien que ie
ne vueille nier, que telle delation ne face naiſtre quel-
que preſumption legiere cõtre celuy, que le mort accu-
ſe {h}. Car iaçoit, que tout homme qui ſ'en va mourir, dit
le Balde, ne ſoit point S. Iean Euangeliſte. Toutesfois
n'eſt il vray ſemblable, qu'il ſoit du tout ſi oublieux,
& peu ſouuenant de ſon ſalut, meſmes en l'extremité
de ſa vie {k}. qu'il vueille denoncer vn autre fauſſemẽt {l}.
I'ay dit notamment quelque legere preſumption: Car
de dire auec quelques vns, que l'aſſertion ſeule du
meurtre, chargeant l'accuſé, fuſt ſuffiſant indice pour la
torture {m}: me ſemble (ie parle touſiours ſous la cenſu
re des plus doctes) n'auoir propos ni apparence. Car
outre que cela manifeſtement contredit, & repugne
aux paroles, & raiſon des loix qui en ont parlé {n}: ſi cela
eſtoit veritable, le bleſſé ſeroit teſmoin en ſa cauſe pro-
pre, contre les deciſions vulgaires {o}: & neantmoins ſon
teſmoignage vaudroit deux: d'autãt que deux teſmoins
ſont deſirez à prouuer vn indice de torture {p}: qui ſeroit
en vn meſme fait, introduire deux choſes ſpeciales, &
par trop irregulieres {q}. Par meſmes raiſons, nous diſons
que ſi vn teſmoin, Iuge, ou Notaire, au dernier ſouſpir
de ſa vie confeſſoit auoir porté faux teſmoignage {r},
prononcé ſentente {ſ}, ou forgé faux inſtrument {t}, par ar-
gent, ou autre eſpece de corruption, il ne leur ſeroit
pourtant donné foy, au preiudice de la partie: à laquel-
le le droit eſtoit ia acquis {u}. Car la confeſſion de celuy,
qui ſ'en va mourir, ne peut nuire, ou preiudicier à au-
truy. Outre qu'il y a grande preſumption au contraire,
que le teſmoin, Iuge, ou Notaire, qui a differé iuſques
à l'article de ſa mort faire telle confeſſion, ne l'aye fai-
te fauſſement, à la ſuggeſtion & ſubornation de quel-
dilectio. Bart. l. iij. P. j. preallegué.
Bal en l'autent. ſi teſtibus. C. de teſtibus. Ange.
